Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — excited to get the hands-on session scheduled. To make scheduling straightforward, here are two delivery options and a short checklist for decisions we need from your side: 

Options
- Onsite full-day (preferred for lab-style routing + AV): 6–8h with morning walkthrough, afternoon load tests and prompt tuning. We can run load tests against a dedicated cluster.
- Hybrid split (remote kickoff + onsite lab half-day): 2h kickoff remote, 3–4h onsite lab. Fewer travel logistics for your broader team.

Key logistics items (please confirm):
1) Preferred date range (we have 6/7, 6/9–6/11 open).
2) Attendee list + headcount for visitor badges.
3) Whether recording/screen-share recording is allowed (some teams require explicit consent).
4) Load test target (concurrent sessions / total tokens) — recommend giving a safety margin.

I attached a draft agenda (Agenda_v1.pdf) and a short access checklist (AccessChecklist.docx). Marissa (cc'd) will own AV/room booking once we confirm date + headcount. Sean is on-thread for production routing/load test sizing.

If helpful, I can propose two calendar invites (onsite vs hybrid) and an SOW/DocuSign link to expedite procurement.

Next steps: please reply with preferred date window and whether you lean onsite or hybrid.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Rachel — thanks, this looks good. Quick clarifications: 
- Headcount: likely 12 on-site (3 infra/3 data science/6 product).
- We prefer hybrid if we can still get the hands-on routing for a subset (i.e., 6 people in the lab, rest remote watching).
- Load test: procurement asked if we can stress to ~500 concurrent sessions (short bursts, 30s–60s each). Is that feasible without needing a formal dedicated cluster purchase?
- Recording: legal wants consent; they're ok with recording if we get an opt-in list and a short consent blurb.
- Procurement contact: procurement@vertexretail.com (cc'd on future SOW/PO requests).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can run the 500 concurrent bursts on a hybrid day or if we should book a dedicated capacity slot?

—Alex

Alex — good questions. Short answers up front: yes, we can support the 500 concurrent bursts; two options depending on risk tolerance:

1) Hybrid + reserved burst (recommended): we provision a short dedicated capacity window during the lab portion (2–3 hours) so those 6 lab users plus remote traffic can hit the same endpoints — gives predictability and avoids throttling on shared hosts. Small incremental cost for the reserved window.

2) Shared-host run with aggressive batching: possible but higher variance in tail latency. Not recommended for evaluating routing/load behavior.

Recording/consent: we can include a one-line consent in the calendar invite and capture opt-ins. I attached a proposed agenda (.ics) we can send as the invite.

Marissa — can you confirm room availability week of 6/7 and whether Lab 3 (capacity for 8) or Conference A (theatre + streaming) is better for hybrid streaming + lab split? Also tag any AV requirements (mics, HDMI capture, internal streaming credentials).

Procurement: happy to send SOW/DocuSign to procurement@vertexretail.com once logistics are locked. I'll attach a one-page SOW for review.

Proposed next steps:
- Alex: confirm date (6/7 or 6/9–6/11) + final attendee list by EOW (2027-05-21).
- Marissa: confirm room + AV and cost estimate for reserved capacity window.
- Sean: prepare a short load-test plan and safety rollback (limit qps, warm cache).

Thanks — I'll hold both pilot invites tentatively until we hear back.

Rachel
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: ProposedAgenda.ics, SOW-Vertex-2027.pdf
